FLOCK & HERD

Thoughtful care for sheep and goats.

Look at the flock, the individual animal and the environment together. Practical observation helps veterinary conversations become more useful.

IN THIS GUIDE

All resources
01

Notice the pattern

Changes in appetite, behaviour, movement or condition are worth recording. Note whether a concern affects one animal, a particular group or the wider flock. Share the timing, recent introductions and relevant management changes with the attending veterinarian.

02

Connect pasture and parasite management

Parasite management in sheep and goats combines veterinary assessment with sanitation, pasture management and attention to animal condition. Faecal testing can support investigation and treatment decisions. Repeated deworming without supporting management can encourage resistance.

03

Keep nutrition and routine in the conversation

Describe the feeding routine, water supply, housing and grazing arrangements when discussing a health concern. These observations provide context; a clinical assessment is still needed to establish the cause of a problem and the appropriate response.

04

Confirm instructions for the exact species

Sheep and goats must not be treated as interchangeable when selecting a medicine. Check the exact product’s authorised species, concentration, route and prescribing instructions. Keep treatment records and any applicable food-chain restrictions traceable.
